arthritis at slaughter was significantly associated with high clinical signs for lactating sows in the farrowing unit, open partitions between the weaning pens and a high clinical sign score for the finishing pigs in the finishing unit.

the risk of arthritis at slaughter in pigs was increased in herds with high clinical signs in the farrowing units and in herds that had open partitions between the weaning units.

a combination of factors in the farrowing, weaning and finishing unit is associated with a high incidence at slaughter of arthritis in the case herd.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the risk factors for arthritis at slaughter in pigs are associated with the housing and management in the weaning units.

the herds with high incidence of arthritis in the joints at slaughter had higher clinical sign scores for both sows and piglet in the farrowing units and for the pigs in the finishing units, and the herds with low incidence had higher age at weaned and castration and more solid walls in the weaning units.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the risk for developing arthritis is increased when the piglets have a high clinical sign score in the farrowing units and the risk is decreased when the piglets are castrated at an early age, the weaning units have solid walls, the piglets are moved at weaning and the finishing units are properly disinfected.
